statement: The Pareto exponent is the reciprocal mean log excess, with optimized mean log likelihood minus the log mean excess minus one.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{y : Fin n → ℝ} (hy : 0 < BurrHeld.avg y) {a : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) :
    log a - a * BurrHeld.avg y ≤ paretoValue y ∧
      log (BurrHeld.avg y)⁻¹ - (BurrHeld.avg y)⁻¹ * BurrHeld.avg y = paretoValue y

statement: When n k ≤ k + 1, every Burr point at shape k is strictly below the optimized Pareto value.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {y : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hy : 0 < BurrHeld.avg y) {j : Fin n} (hj : y j = 0)
    {k c b : ℝ} (hk : 0 < k) (hc : 0 < c) (hsmall : (n : ℝ) * k ≤ k + 1) :
    likelihood y (k, c, b) < paretoValue y

statement: Increasing power, decreasing first shape and moving the endpoint upwards from below reaches the full Pareto likelihood trace.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {y : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hy : ∀ i, 0 ≤ y i) (hmean : 0 < BurrHeld.avg y) :
    Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ likelihood y ((avg y)⁻¹ / t^2, t^2, t))
      atTop (𝓝 (paretoValue y))

statement: With power and adjusted intercept fixed, the Burr likelihood converges to the Weibull likelihood as the first shape diverges.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) (y : Fin n → ℝ) (c b : ℝ) :
    Tendsto (fun k : ℝ ↦ likelihood y (k, c, b - log k)) atTop (𝓝 (weibullLik y c b))

statement: At fixed Weibull power the intercept is minus the log mean powered observation, yielding the closed-form profile.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) (y : Fin n → ℝ) (c : ℝ) :
    let A := BurrHeld.avg (fun i ↦ exp (c*y i))
    let b := -log A
    weibullLik y c b = log c+c*BurrHeld.avg y-log A-1 ∧
      ∀ a, weibullLik y c a ≤ weibullLik y c b

statement: A positive finite power and finite intercept achieve the largest Weibull value for nonconstant data.
For first shape k ≥ 2n, every Burr likelihood is bounded by the optimal Weibull value plus 2n²/k in mean units.
If the first shape stays in a positive compact interval, every escaping net has likelihood tending to minus infinity.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {y : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hne : ∃ i j, y i ≠ y j) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a ≤ b)
    {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} {p : ι → ℝ × ℝ × ℝ}
    (hp : ∀ᶠ t in l, p t ∈ domain ∧ (p t).1 ∈ Icc a b)
    (hescape : ∀ K : Set (ℝ × ℝ × ℝ), IsCompact K → K ⊆ domain →
      ∀ᶠ t in l, p t ∉ K) :
    Tendsto (fun t ↦ likelihood y (p t)) l atBot

statement: Every likelihood superlevel strictly above both optimized faces lies in a compact subset of the finite domain.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {y : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hne : ∃ i j, y i ≠ y j) (hmean : 0 < BurrHeld.avg y) {j : Fin n} (hj : y j = 0)
    {W M : ℝ} (hW : ∀ c > 0, ∀ b, weibullLik y c b ≤ W)
    (hP : paretoValue y < M) (hWM : W < M) :
    ∃ K : Set (ℝ × ℝ × ℝ), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ domain ∧
      ∀ p ∈ domain, M ≤ likelihood y p → p ∈ K

statement: Every escaping net is eventually below each number strictly greater than the better optimized face.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {y : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hne : ∃ i j, y i ≠ y j) (hmean : 0 < BurrHeld.avg y) {j : Fin n} (hj : y j = 0)
    {W : ℝ} (hW : ∀ c > 0, ∀ b, weibullLik y c b ≤ W)
    {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} {p : ι → ℝ × ℝ × ℝ}
    (hp : ∀ᶠ t in l, p t ∈ domain)
    (hescape : ∀ K : Set (ℝ × ℝ × ℝ), IsCompact K → K ⊆ domain →
      ∀ᶠ t in l, p t ∉ K) {M : ℝ} (hM : max (paretoValue y) W < M) :
    ∀ᶠ t in l, likelihood y (p t) < M
scope: Likelihood upper bound on all escaping nets.

statement: On nonconstant log data, a finite point tying or beating the better optimized face is equivalent to finite attainment.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {y : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hy : ∀ i, 0 ≤ y i) (hne : ∃ i j, y i ≠ y j)
    (hmean : 0 < BurrHeld.avg y) {j : Fin n} (hj : y j = 0)
    {c b : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hW : ∀ d > 0, ∀ a, weibullLik y d a ≤ weibullLik y c b) :
    (∃ p ∈ domain, IsMaxOn (likelihood y) domain p) ↔
      ∃ p ∈ domain, max (paretoValue y) (weibullLik y c b) ≤ likelihood y p

statement: For tied shapes and nonconstant data, every finite likelihood superlevel is contained in a compact feasible set.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {y : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hne : ∃ i j, y i ≠ y j) (M : ℝ) :
    ∃ K : Set (ℝ × ℝ), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ BurrHeld.firstDomain ∧
      ∀ p ∈ BurrHeld.firstDomain, M ≤ likelihood y (p.1,p.1,p.2) → p ∈ K

statement: The tied-shape log-data model has a finite maximizer on every nonconstant sample.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {y : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hne : ∃ i j, y i ≠ y j) :
    ∃ p ∈ BurrHeld.firstDomain,
      IsMaxOn (fun q ↦ likelihood y (q.1,q.1,q.2)) BurrHeld.firstDomain p

statement: For nonconstant positive observations the finite-witness criterion and the compact escape bound apply to the physical Burr coefficients.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) (hne : ∃ i j, x i ≠ x j)
    {j : Fin n} (hj : ∀ i, x j ≤ x i) :
    let y := logExcess x j
    let f := fun p : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ ↦ BurrHeld.logLik x p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2
    let J := BurrHeld.avg (fun i ↦ log (x i))
    ∃ c > 0, ∃ b, (∀ d > 0, ∀ t, weibullLik y d t ≤ weibullLik y c b) ∧
    let B := max (paretoValue y) (weibullLik y c b)
    ((∃ p ∈ physicalDomain, IsMaxOn f physicalDomain p) ↔
      ∃ p ∈ physicalDomain, B-J ≤ f p) ∧
    ∀ M > B, ∃ K : Set (ℝ × ℝ × ℝ), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ physicalDomain ∧
      ∀ p ∈ physicalDomain, M-J ≤ f p → p ∈ K
scope: Nonconstant sample. A nominated sample minimum defines the log-data centering.

statement: With threshold held, the criterion and escape bound use positive excesses and both translated faces, with the log-excess Jacobian.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {μ : ℝ}
    (hx : ∀ i, μ < x i) (hne : ∃ i j, x i ≠ x j)
    {j : Fin n} (hj : ∀ i, x j ≤ x i) :
    let e := ShapeFacesParetoIV.excess x μ
    let y := logExcess e j
    let f := fun p : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ ↦ ShapeFacesParetoIV.logLik x μ p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2
    let J := ∑ i, log (e i)
    ∃ c > 0, ∃ b, (∀ d > 0, ∀ t, weibullLik y d t ≤ weibullLik y c b) ∧
    let B := max (paretoValue y) (weibullLik y c b)
    ((∃ p ∈ physicalDomain, IsMaxOn f physicalDomain p) ↔
      ∃ p ∈ physicalDomain, n*B-J ≤ f p) ∧
    ∀ M > B, ∃ K : Set (ℝ × ℝ × ℝ), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ physicalDomain ∧
      ∀ p ∈ physicalDomain, n*M-J ≤ f p → p ∈ K
scope: Nonconstant sample and held location below every observation.

statement: For nonconstant inverse Burr data the criterion and escape bound use reciprocal observations, reciprocal scale and the transformed likelihood units.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) (hne : ∃ i j, x i ≠ x j)
    {j : Fin n} (hj : ∀ i, x i ≤ x j) :
    let y := logExcess (Transfer.reciprocal x) j
    let f := fun p : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ ↦ ShapeFacesInverseBurr.logLik x p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2
    let J := ∑ i, log (x i)
    ∃ c > 0, ∃ b, (∀ d > 0, ∀ t, weibullLik y d t ≤ weibullLik y c b) ∧
    let B := max (paretoValue y) (weibullLik y c b)
    ((∃ p ∈ physicalDomain, IsMaxOn f physicalDomain p) ↔
      ∃ p ∈ physicalDomain, n*B-J ≤ f p) ∧
    ∀ M > B, ∃ K : Set (ℝ × ℝ × ℝ), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ physicalDomain ∧
      ∀ p ∈ physicalDomain, n*M-J ≤ f p → p ∈ K
scope: Nonconstant sample. A nominated sample maximum defines the reciprocal log-data centering.

statement: On every nonconstant positive sample, paralogistic has a finite maximizer and compact containment at every finite likelihood level.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) (hne : ∃ i j, x i ≠ x j) :
    let f := fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Paralogistic.logLik x p.1 p.2
    (∃ p ∈ Weibull.domain, IsMaxOn f Weibull.domain p) ∧
    ∀ M : ℝ, ∃ K : Set (ℝ × ℝ), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ Weibull.domain ∧
      ∀ p ∈ Weibull.domain, M ≤ f p → p ∈ K

hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ}

hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {v : ℝ} (hv : 0 < v) :
    ¬ BddAbove ((fun p : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ ↦
      BurrHeld.logLik (fun _ : Fin n ↦ v) p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2) '' physicalDomain)

hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {v : ℝ} (hv : 0 < v) :

statement: At least half the sample at the minimum strictly excludes every finite Burr point relative to the optimized Pareto value.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {y : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hy : ∀ i, 0 ≤ y i) (hmean : 0 < BurrHeld.avg y)
    (hw : (n : ℝ) / 2 ≤ ((Finset.univ.filter (fun i ↦ y i = 0)).card : ℝ))
    {p : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ} (hp : p ∈ domain) :
    likelihood y p < paretoValue y

statement: For two distinct log levels, a majority at the lower level, including equality, strictly excludes all finite Burr points.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {y : Fin n → ℝ} {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r)
    (hy : ∀ i, y i = 0 ∨ y i = r) (hmean : 0 < BurrHeld.avg y)
    (hw : (n : ℝ) / 2 ≤ ((Finset.univ.filter (fun i ↦ y i = 0)).card : ℝ))
    {p : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ} (hp : p ∈ domain) :
    likelihood y p < paretoValue y

statement: At least half the nonconstant sample at the minimum gives the optimized Pareto supremum in physical likelihood units, strictly above every finite point.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) (hne : ∃ i j, x i ≠ x j)
    {j : Fin n} (hj : ∀ i, x j ≤ x i)
    (hm : (n : ℝ) / 2 ≤ ((Finset.univ.filter (fun i ↦ x i = x j)).card : ℝ)) :
    let f := fun p : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ ↦ BurrHeld.logLik x p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2
    let P := paretoValue (logExcess x j)-BurrHeld.avg (fun i ↦ log (x i))
    sSup (f '' physicalDomain) = P ∧ ∀ p ∈ physicalDomain, f p < P

statement: With threshold held, a majority at the minimum gives the unattained shifted-Pareto supremum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {μ : ℝ}
    (hx : ∀ i, μ < x i) (hne : ∃ i j, x i ≠ x j)
    {j : Fin n} (hj : ∀ i, x j ≤ x i)
    (hm : (n : ℝ) / 2 ≤ ((Finset.univ.filter (fun i ↦ x i = x j)).card : ℝ)) :
    let e := ShapeFacesParetoIV.excess x μ
    let f := fun p : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ ↦ ShapeFacesParetoIV.logLik x μ p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2
    let P := n*paretoValue (logExcess e j)-∑ i, log (e i)
    sSup (f '' physicalDomain) = P ∧ ∀ p ∈ physicalDomain, f p < P

statement: A majority at the maximum gives the unattained upper-endpoint power supremum for inverse Burr.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) (hne : ∃ i j, x i ≠ x j)
    {j : Fin n} (hj : ∀ i, x i ≤ x j)
    (hm : (n : ℝ) / 2 ≤ ((Finset.univ.filter (fun i ↦ x i = x j)).card : ℝ)) :
    let y := logExcess (Transfer.reciprocal x) j
    let f := fun p : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ ↦ ShapeFacesInverseBurr.logLik x p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2
    let P := n*paretoValue y-∑ i, log (x i)
    sSup (f '' physicalDomain) = P ∧ ∀ p ∈ physicalDomain, f p < P

statement: The stated two-level family includes an exact sample at which global maximizers exist on both sides of shape 1/10000.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
:
    ∃ K ∈ Ioo (7/5 : ℝ) (8/5),
      let x : Fin 10000 → ℝ := fun i ↦ if i = 0 then 1 else exp (100000000*K)
      let f := fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Paralogistic.logLik x p.1 p.2
      ∃ p ∈ Weibull.domain, ∃ q ∈ Weibull.domain,
        p.1 < 1/10000 ∧ 1/10000 < q.1 ∧
        IsMaxOn f Weibull.domain p ∧ IsMaxOn f Weibull.domain q
scope: Proves at least two maximizers in the source family. Exact cardinality and uniqueness of the crossing remain open.
